chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Ḥasan al-Luʾluʾī, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Saʿd ibn Abī Khalaf, who said:

I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام say: Ghusl is in fourteen situations; one is obligatory, and the rest are sunnah. The meaning of this is that one of them is obligatory by the outward meaning of the Qur'an, even though there are other ghusls whose obligation is known through the sunnah.

key_terms.أَغْسَالٌ: multiple ritual baths prescribed for different circumstances
key_terms.الْغُسْلُ: ritual bath required or recommended in specific legal situations
key_terms.بِالسُّنَّةِ: through the sunnah (prophetic tradition), as a source of legal knowledge
key_terms.بِظَاهِرِ الْقُرْآنِ: by the apparent wording or outward indication of the Qur'an
key_terms.سُنَّةٌ: a legislated practice established through the Prophetic and Imamic tradition
key_terms.فَرِيضَةٌ: an obligatory ruling that must be observed

ai.seo_question: Which ghusls are obligatory in Islam according to the Qur'an and the sunnah?
ai.summary: This hadith states that ghusl applies in fourteen situations, with one being established as obligatory by the outward wording of the Qur'an, while other obligatory ghusls are known through the sunnah. It highlights the juristic distinction between what is proven directly by the Qur'an and what is established through transmitted hadith.
